title: The dimorphic diaspore model Aethionema arabicum (Brassicaceae): Distinct molecular and morphological control of responses to parental and germination temperatures
authors: Chandler JO; Wilhelmsson PK; Fernandez-Pozo N; Graeber K; Arshad W; Pérez M; Steinbrecher T; Ullrich KK; Nguyen T; Mérai Z; Mummenhoff K; Theißen G; Strnad M; Scheid OM; Schranz ME; Petřík I; Tarkowská D; Novák O; Rensing SA; Leubner-Metzger G
one_liner_zh: 该文研究植物双态繁殖体对温度的分子与激素响应，虽涉及转录因子表达，但无蛋白质-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract:
Plants in habitats with unpredictable conditions are often characterized by diversifying their bet-hedging strategies that ensure fitness over a wider range of variable environmental factors. A striking example is the diaspore (seed and fruit) heteromorphism that evolved to maximize species survival in Aethionema arabicum (Brassicaceae) in which external and endogenous triggers allow the production of two distinct diaspores on the same plant. Using this dimorphic diaspore model, we identified contrasting molecular, biophysical, and ecophysiological mechanisms in the germination responses to different temperatures of the mucilaginous seeds (M + seed morphs), the dispersed indehiscent fruits (IND fruit morphs), and the bare non-mucilaginous M − seeds obtained by pericarp (fruit coat) removal from IND fruits. Large-scale comparative transcriptome and hormone analyses of M + seeds, IND fruits, and M − seeds provided comprehensive datasets for their distinct thermal responses. Morph-specific differences in co-expressed gene modules in seeds, as well as seed and pericarp hormone contents identified a role of the IND pericarp in imposing coat dormancy by generating hypoxia affecting ABA sensitivity. This involved expression of morph-specific transcription factors, hypoxia response and cell wall-remodeling genes, as well as altered abscisic acid (ABA) metabolism, transport, and signaling. Parental temperature affected ABA contents and ABA-related gene expression and altered IND pericarp biomechanical properties. Elucidating the molecular framework underlying the diaspore heteromorphism can provide insight into developmental responses to globally changing temperatures.

IN A NUTSHELL

Background

Heteromorphic diaspores (fruits and seeds) are an adaptive bet-hedging strategy to ensure survival in spatiotemporally variable environments. The stone cress Aethionema arabicum , an annual plant native to semi-arid habitats in Anatolia (Turkey), one of the world’s hotspots of biodiversity. It is a close relative of Arabidopsis, rapeseed, cabbage and other Brassica crops, but in contrast to these Ae. arabicum disperses two distinct diaspores from the same plant. These dimorphic diaspores are the mucilaginous seeds (dispersed by pod shatter) and indehiscent fruits (dispersed by abscission). The wing-like pericarp (fruit coat) of the single-seeded indehiscent fruit allows wind dispersal over large distances. The amounts and ratios of the dimorphic diaspores are variable and depend on the environmental conditions. The dimorphic diaspores differ in morphology, dormancy and germination properties and thereby make Ae. arabicum an excellent model for the comparative investigation of the underpinning molecular mechanisms.

Question

We asked how temperature during fruit and seed formation and during seed germination affect dormancy release and germination speed, and how the morphology, hormonal regulation, and the expression of genes differ between the dimorphic diaspores.

Findings

Large-scale comparative transcriptome and hormone analyses of the mucilaginous seeds and the indehiscent fruits, as well as the seeds artificially extracted from indehiscent fruits by pericarp (fruit coat) removal, provided comprehensive datasets for their distinct thermal responses. Material obtained from plants grown at different temperatures during reproduction was imbibed at different temperatures for germination. This altered the abscisic acid (ABA) metabolism and the pericarp biomechanical properties. Diaspore-specific differences in response to distinct imbibition temperatures identified distinct gene expression patterns in seeds, distinct seed and pericarp hormone contents, and a role of the pericarp in generating hypoxia inside the fruit and imposing coat dormancy. This revealed distinct combinations of specific transcription factors, hypoxia responses and cell wall-remodeling genes, as well as altered signaling pathway genes.

Next steps

Our large-scale comparative transcriptome datasets are easily and publicly accessible via the Aethionema arabicum web portal ( https://plantcode.cup.uni-freiburg.de/aetar_db/index.php ). We plan to expand this by future work on seedlings derived from the dimorphic diaspores, by comparing different Ae. arabicum genotypes, and by studying responses to specific stresses. Understanding the molecular basis of this fascinating example of developmental diversity and plasticity and its regulation by temperature is expected to add insight how plants respond to changing environmental conditions.
abstract_zh:
生活在不可预测环境中的植物，往往通过多样化其赌注分散策略（bet-hedging strategies）来确保在更广泛的可变环境因素下保持适应性。一个显著的例子是二型性繁殖体（diaspore，即种子和果实）异型性，这种特性在阿拉伯芥（*Aethionema arabicum*，十字花科）中进化以最大化物种生存，其中外部和内源触发因素使得同一植株上产生两种不同的繁殖体。利用这种二型性繁殖体模型，我们鉴定了在萌发响应不同温度时，粘液种子（M+种子形态）、散落的闭果（IND果实形态）以及通过去除IND果实果皮（果壳）获得的裸露非粘液M−种子之间对比鲜明的分子、生物物理和生态生理机制。大规模比较转录组和激素分析为M+种子、IND果实和M−种子提供了其不同温度响应的全面数据集。种子中共表达基因模块的形态特异性差异，以及种子和果皮激素含量，揭示了IND果皮通过产生缺氧环境来施加种皮休眠并影响ABA敏感性的作用。这涉及形态特异性转录因子、缺氧响应和细胞壁重塑基因的表达，以及脱落酸（ABA）代谢、运输和信号传导的改变。亲本温度影响ABA含量和ABA相关基因表达，并改变IND果皮的生物力学特性。阐明繁殖体异型性背后的分子框架，可以为理解全球温度变化下的发育响应提供见解。

概要

背景

异型繁殖体（果实和种子）是一种适应性赌注分散策略，以确保在时空变化的环境中生存。石芥花（*Aethionema arabicum*）是一种一年生植物，原产于安纳托利亚（土耳其）的半干旱栖息地，该地区是世界生物多样性热点之一。它是拟南芥、油菜、卷心菜及其他芸苔属作物的近亲，但与这些物种不同，*Ae. arabicum* 从同一植株上散布两种不同的繁殖体。这些二型性繁殖体是粘液种子（通过荚果开裂散布）和闭果（通过离层脱落散布）。单种子闭果的翼状果皮（果壳）允许风力远距离传播。二型性繁殖体的数量和比例是可变的，取决于环境条件。二型性繁殖体在形态、休眠和萌发特性上存在差异，从而使 *Ae. arabicum* 成为比较研究其潜在分子机制的优良模型。

问题

我们探讨了果实和种子形成期间以及种子萌发期间的温度如何影响休眠释放和萌发速度，以及二型性繁殖体之间的形态、激素调控和基因表达有何差异。

发现

大规模比较转录组和激素分析，针对粘液种子、闭果以及通过去除果皮（果壳）从闭果中人工提取的种子，提供了其不同温度响应的全面数据集。在繁殖期间于不同温度下生长的植株所获得的材料，在不同温度下吸水萌发。这改变了脱落酸（ABA）代谢和果皮生物力学特性。对不同吸水温度的响应中，繁殖体特异性差异揭示了种子中不同的基因表达模式、种子和果皮中不同的激素含量，以及果皮在果实内部产生缺氧环境并施加种皮休眠中的作用。这揭示了特定转录因子、缺氧响应和细胞壁重塑基因的不同组合，以及信号通路基因的改变。

下一步

我们的大规模比较转录组数据集可通过 *Aethionema arabicum* 网络门户（ https://plantcode.cup.uni-freiburg.de/aetar_db/index.php ）轻松公开访问。我们计划通过未来对二型性繁殖体来源幼苗的研究、比较不同 *Ae. arabicum* 基因型以及研究对特定胁迫的响应来扩展这项工作。理解这一发育多样性和可塑性及其受温度调控的迷人实例的分子基础，有望为植物如何响应变化的环境条件提供见解。
